title: Integrated Machine Learning, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Design Novel Peptide Inhibitors of Rabies Virus Glycoprotein

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rabies is the most lethal viral zoonotic diseases worldwide. The study aimed to develop novel anti-viral agents targeting the rabies virus glycoprotein (RABV-G), which mediates host cell recognition and viral entry.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A computational peptide design strategy was employed to design peptide inhibitors against RABV-G. Peptide sequences were designed from the receptor binding region of α-bungarotoxin through mutation and optimisation while eliminating neurotoxic properties.
analysis.methods: A hybrid machine learning-deep framework was used for toxicity screening. The selected non-toxic peptides were analysed through framework of different tools for Physiochemical characterization, antiviral activity prediction, molecular docking, binding affinity and molecular dynamic simulation were performed to analyse peptide RABV-G interactions.
analysis.main_results: Among the evaluated candidates, MKMKCHTTATMKIV (P40) shown the most favourable docking with a HADDOCK scores − 90 ± 3.8, and binding free energy of -10.3kcal/mol, followed by CLDLGYTIVCHTTATSPI (P3), MKIVCHTTATSPMKV (P21), and MKIVCHTTMKSPMK (P25).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study design shows the α-bungarotoxin derived peptides can target RABV-G and P440 can be promising lead candidate for development of peptide-based drug delivery.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of peptide-based drug delivery systems for targeting rabies virus glycoprotein, potentially leading to new therapeutic strategies for rabies infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on computational methods and does not include experimental validation, which limits the confidence in the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on in silico analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop novel anti-viral agents targeting the rabies virus glycoprotein (RABV-G), which is critical for host cell recognition and viral entry. A computational peptide design strategy was used to generate sequences from the receptor binding region of α-bungarotoxin, optimizing them to eliminate neurotoxic properties. The selected peptides were analyzed using a hybrid machine learning-deep framework for toxicity screening and further evaluated through physiochemical characterization, antiviral activity prediction, molecular docking, binding affinity, and molecular dynamic simulations. The results showed that MKMKCHTTATMKIV (P40) had the most favorable docking with RABV-G, followed by other candidates. The study suggests that these α-bungarotoxin-derived peptides could be promising lead candidates for developing peptide-based therapies against rabies. However, the reliance on computational methods without experimental validation limits the confidence in the findings, and the evidence strength is considered moderate.

title: Peptide-targeted cubosome and hexosome nanoassemblies mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in a MitoPark model.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a primary pathogenic mechanism underlying dopaminergic neuron loss in the nigrostriatal pathway in Parkinson's disease (PD). The study aimed to explore mitochondrion-targeted therapeutic strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized the MitoPark mouse model, in which mitochondrial transcription factor A (Tfam) is selectively ablated in midbrain dopamine neurons, resulting in progressive neurodegeneration. The research focused on evaluating the effects of peptide-targeted nanoassemblies in this model.
analysis.methods: The researchers designed multifunctional lyotropic liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) of the cubosome and hexosome types for noninvasive nose-to-brain delivery. These nanocarriers were engineered with lipids essential for membrane integrity (plasmalogens and ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs)) and a nonlamellar structural lipid (monoolein).
analysis.main_results: In vitro studies using differentiated SH-SY5Y cells subjected to oxidative stress demonstrated that the targeted LNPs enhanced cellular uptake and activated key neuroprotective signaling cascades, including AKT, ERK, and STAT3 phosphorylation. In vivo, intranasal administration of the optimized LNPs in MitoPark mice was associated with a trend toward the preservation of dopaminergic neuronal markers (such as tyrosine hydroxylase) and the regulation of mitochondrial-related proteins such as ATP5A1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish peptide-targeted, therapeutic lipid (plasmalogen/PUFA)-based nanoassemblies as a potent nonviral platform for noninvasive nose-to-brain delivery that may modulate mitochondrial- and neurodegeneration-related signaling pathways in a genetic model of PD.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the potential of nonviral nanoassemblies for modulating mitochondrial dysfunction and neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease, which could inform future therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in vitro and in vivo models, which may not fully represent human conditions. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of direct clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of peptide-targeted nanoassemblies to mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in a Parkinson's disease model. The researchers designed cubosome and hexosome nanoparticles with specific lipids and neuroprotective agents to enhance neuronal uptake and activation of protective signaling pathways. In vitro and in vivo results showed improved cellular uptake and trends toward preservation of dopaminergic markers and regulation of mitochondrial proteins. The findings suggest these nanoassemblies could be a promising nonviral platform for targeting mitochondrial dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases. However, the study's reliance on animal models limits its direct applicability to human conditions, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: Environmental DNA and next-generation sequencing for post-elimination surveillance of neglected tropical diseases in the Philippines and the Western Pacific Region

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease, with an emphasis on post-elimination surveillance strategies in the Philippines and the Western Pacific Region. The central question is how to effectively detect and monitor rabies in low-prevalence, focal transmission settings using environmental DNA and next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of evidence on targeted and metagenomic NGS approaches for detecting rabies virus in environmental matrices, vectors, intermediate hosts, and animal reservoirs. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods, but it outlines the general framework for integrating NGS with surveillance objectives and resource constraints.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that environmental NGS has the potential to transform post-elimination rabies surveillance, particularly in resource-limited settings. It highlights the need for frameworks that go beyond assay sensitivity and specificity to address how surveillance objectives, low-prevalence conditions, sampling strategy, and resource constraints jointly determine what can realistically be detected.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a key gap in the integration of environmental signals with infection prevalence and other biological data. It also notes that while NGS-based wastewater surveillance has shown promise during the COVID-19 pandemic, environmental NGS remains underutilized for neglected tropical diseases like rabies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing operational frameworks for deploying environmental genomic surveillance in post-elimination settings. It also highlights the importance of linking environmental signals with vector, host, and clinical data to guide programmatic decisions aligned with the 2030 NTD road map.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of environmental DNA and next-generation sequencing (NGS) for post-elimination rabies surveillance in the Philippines and the Western Pacific Region. It identifies the limitations of conventional diagnostic tools in low-prevalence settings and argues for the need of integrated frameworks that combine NGS with surveillance objectives and resource constraints. The review highlights the potential of NGS-based wastewater surveillance, as demonstrated during the COVID-19 pandemic, but notes its underutilization for rabies. It emphasizes the importance of calibrating environmental signals with infection prevalence and other biological data to support programmatic decisions in line with the 2030 NTD road map.

title: Determinants of rabies knowledge, attitudes, and practices among secondary and vocational school students in Maha Sarakham Province, Thailand

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines rabies virus and rabies disease, focusing on knowledge, attitudes, and preventive practices (KAP) among secondary and vocational school students in Maha Sarakham Province, Thailand, in 2023. The central question addresses determinants of rabies KAP in this specific population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is an analytic cross-sectional survey conducted from January to May 2023 with 628 participants. Data were collected via online and on-site questionnaires, and both descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed to identify factors associated with rabies KAP.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Most participants demonstrated moderate knowledge (55.89%), neutral attitudes (81.37%), and moderate preventive practices (72.77%) toward rabies. Students with experience raising animals, prior study of zoonotic diseases, a history of animal bites or scratches, or rabies vaccination had significantly higher knowledge and practice scores (p < 0.05). Knowledge and attitudes were positively correlated with preventive practices (r = 0.14 and r = 0.28, respectively; p < 0.05).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report heterogeneity in KAP outcomes across different demographic subgroups beyond the reported associations. The review does not address potential biases in self-reported data or the generalizability of findings to other regions or populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the need for targeted rabies awareness programs in schools and colleges, focusing on risk of rabies, modes of transmission, first aid, health-seeking behavior after animal bites, and preventive measures for pets and community animals.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates rabies knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) among secondary and vocational school students in Maha Sarakham, Thailand, in 2023. The cross-sectional survey of 628 students found moderate knowledge, neutral attitudes, and moderate preventive practices toward rabies. Students with animal-raising experience, prior zoonotic disease education, animal bite history, or rabies vaccination exhibited significantly higher knowledge and practice scores. Knowledge and attitudes correlated positively with preventive practices. The review underscores the urgent need for school-based rabies awareness programs addressing transmission risks, first aid, and preventive measures for pets and community animals.

title: Primary healthcare facilities readiness for animal-related injuries: Availability, stock-Outs, and affordability of essential commodities in rural public health facilities, Tanzania

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the availability, stockouts, and affordability of essential commodities for managing animal-related injuries in rural Tanzanian healthcare facilities, as these injuries are often preventable with timely access to safe and effective medications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted in February 2024, analyzing data from 29 public primary healthcare facilities in Mkinga District, Tanga region, covering the period from 2019 to 2023.
analysis.methods: The availability, stockouts, and affordability of 33 essential health commodities were extracted from hospital pharmaceutical ledgers. Affordability was calculated using the wage of the lowest-paid government worker per day as a benchmark.
analysis.main_results: Overall availability of essential commodities remained below the WHO target of > 80%, with dispensaries more affected than health centers. Notable incremental availability was observed in 2023, but disparities persisted, particularly for snake antivenom (34.6% vs 100%) and antirabies (23.1% vs 66.7%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the persistent inadequacy of essential commodities for managing animal-related injuries in rural Tanzanian facilities, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to improve access and reduce preventable deaths.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the critical importance of strengthening supply chain systems, forecasting, and financing mechanisms to ensure equitable access to life-saving commodities for animal-related injuries in rural areas.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on historical facility data, which may not reflect current conditions. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on a single district and does not account for broader regional or national trends.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the availability, stockouts, and affordability of essential health commodities for managing animal-related injuries in rural Tanzanian primary healthcare facilities. It reveals that most commodities remain below WHO availability targets, with significant disparities between dispensaries and health centers. Affordability is also a major issue, as nearly all commodities exceed the 7% affordability threshold. The findings highlight the need for improved supply chain systems and sustainable financing to ensure equitable access to life-saving treatments. While the study provides valuable insights, its reliance on historical data and limited geographic scope may affect the generalizability of the results.

title: Antigen presentation by CD40+MHC-II+ astrocytes promotes CNS autoimmunity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of astrocytes in promoting CNS autoimmunity, particularly focusing on their functional interactions with CD4+ T cells in the context of diseases like multiple sclerosis and its mouse model, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using a combination of rabies barcode interaction detection followed by sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, in vitro co-culture systems, and in vivo CRISPR-Cas9-based genetic perturbation studies. It involved analyzing astrocyte-interacting CD4+ T cells in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis models and examining astrocytes in multiple sclerosis samples.
analysis.methods: Additionally, in vivo subproteomic approaches and AlphaFold-Multimer predictions were employed to study the molecular mechanisms of CD40 activation in astrocytes.
analysis.main_results: The study found that direct astrocyte-CD4+ T cell interactions enhance pathogenic T helper 17 cell responses in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis. It also demonstrated that CD40 activation in astrocytes by CD40L from CD4+ T cells leads to the accumulation of PLIN4-positive lipid droplets, which support p65 acetylation-dependent NF-κB activation and antigen presentation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as defining a previously unrecognized mechanism by which astrocytes promote CNS autoimmunity through CD40 and MHC-II expression, highlighting the role of lipid droplets in facilitating antigen presentation and NF-κB activation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings have significant implications for understanding the pathogenesis of CNS autoimmunity and could inform future research on the role of astrocytes in autoimmune diseases, potentially leading to new therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on experimental models and in vivo techniques, which may limit its generalizability to human conditions. The findings are supported by multiple methods, including sequencing and genetic perturbation, providing moderate confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how CD40+MHC-II+ astrocytes contribute to CNS autoimmunity by promoting pathogenic T helper 17 cell responses in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis. Using advanced techniques like rabies barcode interaction detection, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in vivo CRISPR-Cas9-based genetic perturbation, the research identifies a novel mechanism involving CD40 activation and lipid droplet accumulation. The findings suggest that these astrocytes facilitate antigen presentation and NF-κB activation, which are critical for autoimmunity. The study's implications could guide future research on autoimmune diseases and their treatment. However, the reliance on experimental models may limit the direct applicability of the results to human conditions, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: Rabies viral RNA and antibody response after post-exposure prophylaxis: Implications for blood donor deferral

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess rabies real-time RT-PCR status and serological responses among post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) recipients at various intervals following treatment and to consider whether these findings might justify a re-examination of the current one-year blood donor deferral policy after anti-rabies treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a single-center interventional study at an anti-rabies clinic in a tertiary hospital in North India. The study enrolled twenty immunologically naïve adults who had sustained category III animal bites, with no prior rabies exposure or treatment, and who adhered fully to the protocol. Participants received anti-rabies vaccines and equine rabies immunoglobulin as appropriate for their category.
analysis.methods: Blood samples were collected 48 to 120 days after exposure and tested for rabies viral RNA using real-time RT-PCR and for rabies antibody levels using ELISA. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, percentile analysis, correlation analysis, and regression analysis, as appropriate.
analysis.main_results: All participants tested negative using RT-PCR, indicating no detectable rabies viral RNA. ELISA titers ranged from 0.881 to 4.449 IU/mL, and all participants exceeded the protective threshold of 0.5 IU/mL.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that individuals who complete appropriate anti-rabies post-exposure prophylaxis may not have detectable circulating viral RNA and maintain protective antibody responses during follow-up.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support a more evidence-based reconsideration of the current prolonged blood donor deferral following anti-rabies treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence supporting such a long deferral period is limited, and larger multicenter studies are needed.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated rabies viral RNA and antibody responses in individuals who received post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) following category III animal bites. Twenty immunologically naïve adults were enrolled and followed up between 48 and 120 days post-exposure. All participants tested negative for rabies viral RNA using real-time RT-PCR and had antibody titers above the protective threshold. These results suggest that PEP recipients may not require a one-year blood donor deferral, as they show no detectable viral RNA and maintain protective antibody levels. However, the study's limited sample size and single-center design highlight the need for larger, multicenter studies to confirm these findings. The findings could inform more evidence-based policies for blood donor deferral after anti-rabies treatment.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides a detailed description of the epidemiological characteristics of animal bite and scratch injuries in a large urban hospital in Hangzhou, China, and identifies routinely recorded factors associated with WHO category III exposure.

title: A Correlational Study to Assess the Prevalence of Dog Bite Among Children and Awareness of Prevention and Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Among Parents at Selected Community, Bangalore

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dog bites are a major public health concern worldwide, especially in underdeveloped nations where rabies is still endemic. The study aimed to address the lack of awareness about prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis among parents.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted to assess the epidemiological profile, management, and outcomes of dog bite cases. The study was carried out at the Emergency Department of BGS GIMS, and data were collected from patients presenting with dog bites between November 2025 and February 2026.
analysis.methods: The study design involved collecting data from patients presenting with dog bites at the Emergency Department of BGS GIMS. The data collection period spanned from November 2025 to February 2026.
analysis.main_results: The study found that dogs are responsible for the great majority of human rabies deaths, accounting for up to 99% of rabies transmission to people.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the critical role of dog bites in rabies transmission and emphasized the need for increased awareness among parents regarding prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies aimed at reducing rabies transmission through dog bite prevention and improving parental awareness of post-exposure prophylaxis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate as it provides a descriptive overview of the issue without detailed statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a descriptive cross-sectional analysis at the Emergency Department of BGS GIMS to assess the prevalence of dog bites among children and parental awareness of prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis. The research highlighted that dogs are responsible for up to 99% of rabies transmission to humans, emphasizing the need for increased awareness among parents. The findings suggest that improving parental knowledge about rabies prevention and post-exposure measures could significantly impact public health outcomes. However, the study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analysis. The results underscore the importance of targeted interventions in communities where rabies remains endemic, particularly focusing on children and their caregivers.

title: The Critical Need for a Comprehensive Post-Exposure Care Bundle following Rabies Exposure: A Report of Two Cases

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rabies is a zoonotic disease that is almost always fatal but can be prevented; it disproportionately affects areas of Asia and Africa with limited resources.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) failures continue to cause avoidable deaths despite advancements in vaccination techniques.
analysis.methods: The supplied evidence does not report how exposure, intervention, measurements and analysis were performed.
analysis.main_results: Two rabies deaths in which vaccination was not enough to prevent death are reported in the current study: one in an adult bitten by a wolf and another in a child bitten on the face by a stray dog.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These incidents underscore the crucial importance of a comprehensive "rabies care bundle" that encompasses active vaccination, passive immunization with RIG, and thorough wound care.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The supplied evidence does not report specific implications for surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, ecology, risk assessment, prevention or future study.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report design limitations, bias, confounding, sample size, controls, generalisability, abstract-only evidence or a justified high/moderate/low assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the critical need for a comprehensive post-exposure care bundle following rabies exposure, as evidenced by two fatal cases where vaccination alone was insufficient. The first case involved an adult bitten by a wolf, while the second case was a child bitten on the face by a stray dog. Both cases revealed critical shortcomings in comprehensive care, such as improper wound suturing, poor wound management, and failure to administer rabies immunoglobulin (RIG). The authors emphasize the importance of a "rabies care bundle" that includes active vaccination, passive immunization with RIG, and thorough wound care. They also stress the need to increase clinician awareness and ensure all PEP components are accessible to prevent similar outcomes and maintain public trust in rabies vaccination programs. The study underscores the importance of adhering to WHO guidelines to improve rabies prevention and treatment strategies. However, the evidence does not provide detailed limitations or a comprehensive assessment of the study's strength.

title: Longitudinal Assessment of Psychological Distress and Coping Strategies in Animal Bite Victims Undergoing Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Animal bites, especially those from dogs, are a significant public health concern, leading to physical injuries and psychological distress.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective, observational study was conducted at a tertiary care anti-rabies clinic in Northern India. Participants (≥12 years of age) with Category II or III animal bites were included. The sample size was 100 participants, accounting for a 20% nonresponse rate.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through sociodemographic questionnaires and psychological assessments (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, Impact of Event Scale–Revised [IES-R], Depression, Anxiety, Stress Scale [DASS-21], and Brief COPE).
analysis.main_results: Psychological distress, as measured via IES-R and DASS-21, decreased significantly over 28 days. Severe Category III bites were associated with higher anxiety and stress.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that psychological distress, including anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder, and depression, improved over time, emphasizing the need for integrated psychological support in rabies PEP protocols, especially in resource-limited settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously inform the importance of integrating psychological support into rabies post-exposure prophylaxis protocols, particularly in resource-limited settings where the psychological burden of severe animal bites is significant.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and does not account for potential confounding factors, which may limit the confidence in causal inferences. The evidence strength is moderate due to the study's design and the potential for unmeasured variables to influence the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the psychological impact of animal bites in individuals undergoing rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). It highlights the significant psychological distress, particularly anxiety and stress, associated with severe Category III bites. The research underscores the need for integrated psychological support in rabies PEP protocols, especially in resource-limited settings. The study was conducted at a tertiary care anti-rabies clinic in Northern India, involving 100 participants. Psychological assessments were used to measure distress levels, which showed a decline over 28 days. The findings suggest that bite severity, age, and socioeconomic status influence distress and coping strategies. However, the study's observational design and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in causal interpretations, resulting in a moderate evidence strength assessment.

title: Community knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding rabies prevention in Kédougou, Senegal, 2022

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rabies remains a public health problem in Senegal, particularly in the Kédougou region, where one rabies-related death was reported in 2019.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Kédougou district using multistage cluster sampling (n = 845) recommended by WHO.
analysis.methods: A structured questionnaire was used to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics as well as rabies-related KAP, with a score cut-off of 80%. Variables with a p-value less than 0.20 were included in a logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Among the 845 participants, 552 (65.3%) were male, with a median age of 40 years [18 to 67 years]. About 25.7% had good knowledge, 19.6% had positive attitudes, and 15.0% reported positive practices towards rabies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Community members who were rabies-aware (aOR = 5.57, CI: 2.46 – 15.1, p = 0.001) and males in the community (aOR = 2.54, CI: 1.27-5.65, p = 0.007) had better rabies preventive practices compared to those who were not rabies aware and their female counterparts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study highlighted significant shortcomings in the KAPs in terms of rabies prevention. In order to reduce these gaps, awareness campaigns have been organised, focusing on the communication of the risks associated with this disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess community knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding rabies prevention in Kédougou, Senegal, in 2022. A cross-sectional survey using multistage cluster sampling was conducted among 845 participants. The findings revealed that only 25.7% had good knowledge, 19.6% had positive attitudes, and 15.0% reported positive practices towards rabies. Rabies-aware individuals and males were found to have better preventive practices. The study concluded that there are significant gaps in KAPs related to rabies prevention, emphasizing the need for targeted awareness campaigns. The evidence is based on survey data and statistical analysis, but no limitations or evidence strength were explicitly reported.
